products.name: Langfuse
products.note: Open-source, framework-agnostic LLM observability: tracing, prompt management, evals, datasets; OpenTelemetry-native; acquired by ClickHouse

reading.body:
Langfuse is an open-source platform for tracing, monitoring, and evaluating LLM applications, adopted by over 50,000 companies and processing billions of observations monthly.

LLM systems generate far more observability data than traditional software: every prompt, completion, retrieval step, and tool call produces rich structured output that legacy monitoring tools cannot handle at scale. Langfuse addresses this by capturing hierarchical traces of the full execution path, allowing teams to debug, cost-optimize, and improve applications across frameworks like LangChain, Claude Agents, and Vertex AI. The platform's framework-agnostic design and OpenTelemetry compliance mean it can work across the fragmented tooling landscape that AI engineering has inherited.

For AI infrastructure, observability is already critical to the binding constraints: as models grow and systems scale, understanding where compute is spent—which prompts are expensive, which retrieval steps fail, which inference patterns waste tokens—becomes inseparable from optimization. A platform that operates at billions of observations per month is operating at the scale where decisions about inference cost and latency compound across thousands of applications.

The data does not cover pricing, deployment options, or the technical performance of Langfuse relative to alternatives. It also does not explain the scope of work ClickHouse's acquisition represents or how it affects the platform's independence or roadmap.

profile_text.body:
Langfuse describes itself as an open-source AI engineering platform for building, monitoring, and improving LLM applications. Its site says it covers tracing, prompt management, evaluations, and analytics dashboards, and that hierarchical traces capture every LLM call, tool invocation, and retrieval step, with filtering by user, session, cost, latency, or custom metadata. The company states it is used by 50,000+ companies and processes billions of observations per month. It lists integrations with frameworks and platforms including Claude Code, LiteLLM, LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, and others.

Langfuse is listed as an AI governance and risk management platform product. It is described as open-source, framework-agnostic LLM observability covering tracing, prompt management, evals, and datasets, OpenTelemetry-native, and acquired by ClickHouse.
